'''Carlo Catassi''' (born 19 April 1953) is an Italian [[Pediatric gastroenterology|pediatric gastroenterologist]] and [[Epidemiology|epidemiologist]]. He is a [[professor]] at the [[Università Politecnica delle Marche]] in [[Ancona]], [[Italy]], where he leads the Department of Pediatrics and directs the Pediatric Residency Program.<ref name="UPM">[https://www.univpm.it/ Università Politecnica delle Marche – Official Website]</ref> He is also a visiting scientist at [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in [[Boston]], [[United States]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Center for Celiac Research Directors Update Celiac Disease Landscape |url=https://www.beyondceliac.org/research-news/center-for-celiac-research-directors-update-celiac-disease-landscape/ |website=Beyond Celiac |access-date=25 April 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Catassi has held a full professorship at the [[Università Politecnica delle Marche]] since 1993. From 2013 to 2016, he served as president of the Italian Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (SIGENP).<ref>{{cite web |title=SIGENP Presidents |url=https://www.sigenp.org/ |website=SIGENP |language=it |access-date=25 April 2025}}</ref>

In the 1990s, he coordinated a multicenter screening in Italy that helped shape the "celiac iceberg" model, illustrating how many individuals with [[celiac disease]] remain undiagnosed.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Catassi |first=Carlo |title=The coeliac iceberg in Italy. A multicentre antigliadin antibodies screening... |journal=Acta Paediatrica |date=1996 |volume=412 |pages=29–35 |doi=10.1111/j.1651-2227.1996.tb14244.x |pmid=8783752|hdl=11380/648718 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> He later led one of the first population-based screening studies in the United States, which estimated the disease affects roughly 1% of the population.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Catassi |first=Carlo |title=Detection of Celiac Disease in Primary Care: A Multicenter Case-Finding Study in North America |journal=Am J Gastroenterol |year=2007 |volume=102 |issue=7 |pages=1454–1460 |doi=10.1111/j.1572-0241.2007.01173.x |pmid=17355413}}</ref>

His research extended globally, including studies in [[Brazil]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Gandolfi |first=L. |title=Prevalence of celiac disease among blood donors in Brazil |journal=Am J Gastroenterol |date=2000 |volume=95 |issue=3 |pages=689–692 |doi=10.1111/j.1572-0241.2000.01847.x |pmid=10710058}}</ref> and [[Middle Eastern]] populations, where he contributed to early data on disease prevalence.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Rostami |first=K. |title=Coeliac disease in Middle Eastern countries... |journal=Digestive and Liver Disease |volume=36 |issue=10 |pages=694–697 |year=2004 |doi=10.1016/j.dld.2004.05.010 |pmid=15506671}}</ref>

==Research==
Catassi’s research focuses on the epidemiology and clinical management of gluten-related disorders. He conducted one of the first clinical trials to determine how much [[gluten]] can safely be tolerated by individuals with celiac disease. These results helped set the international regulatory limit of 20 ppm for gluten-free products.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Catassi |first=Carlo |title=A prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to establish a safe gluten threshold... |journal=Am J Clin Nutr |year=2007 |volume=85 |issue=1 |pages=160–166 |doi=10.1093/ajcn/85.1.160 |pmid=17209192|doi-access=free }}</ref>

He has also examined high-prevalence populations, including the [[Saharawis|Saharawi people]], among whom celiac disease rates were observed to be around 6%.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Teresi |first=Saverio |title=Celiac disease seropositivity in Saharawi children... |journal=J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr |year=2010 |volume=50 |issue=5 |pages=506–509 |doi=10.1097/MPG.0b013e3181bab30c |pmid=20639708}}</ref>

In collaboration with international experts, Catassi co-developed the Salerno criteria for diagnosing [[non-celiac gluten sensitivity]] (NCGS), aiming to improve diagnostic consistency.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Catassi |first=Carlo |title=Diagnosis of Non-Celiac Gluten Sensitivity (NCGS)... |journal=Nutrients |volume=7 |issue=6 |pages=4966–4977 |year=2015 |doi=10.3390/nu7064966 |doi-access=free |pmid=26096570 |pmc=4488826}}</ref>

His studies also examined environmental triggers of celiac disease in children, showing that neither the timing of gluten introduction nor breastfeeding significantly impacts disease risk.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Lionetti |first=Elena |title=Introduction of gluten, HLA status, and the risk of celiac disease in children |journal=N Engl J Med |year=2014 |volume=371 |issue=14 |pages=1295–1303 |doi=10.1056/NEJMoa1400697 |pmid=25271602|hdl=2318/155238 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Catassi C, et al. "Detection of Celiac Disease in Primary Care: A Multicenter Case-Finding Study in North America." ''[[The American Journal of Gastroenterology]]'', 2007. {{doi|10.1111/j.1572-0241.2007.01173.x}}.
* Catassi C, et al. "A prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to establish a safe gluten threshold..." ''[[The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition]]'', 2007. {{doi|10.1093/ajcn/85.1.160}}.
* Catassi C, et al. "Diagnosis of Non-Celiac Gluten Sensitivity (NCGS): The Salerno Experts' Criteria." ''[[Nutrients (journal)|Nutrients]]'', 2015. {{doi|10.3390/nu7064966|doi-access=free}}.

==Personal life==
Catassi is married to Dr. Eleonora Bove, a lawyer. They have two children.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}
